headline: Spanish 102 Master
threshold: Expand Spanish 101 through past narration, objects, plans, requests, commands and introductory subjunctive choices.

lessons.title: Retell a journey with causes
lessons.objective: Retell a journey with causes: Use the preterite for bounded events and connectors to order them; time words provide context.

words.es: Ayer llegué tarde a la estación.
words.en: Yesterday I arrived late at the station.
First I looked for the correct exit.
Then I bought a one-way ticket.

words.es: El tren salió a las ocho.
Llamé a Elena y expliqué el problema.
words.en: I called Elena and explained the problem.
In the end we took a bus.

words.es: Al contar la historia, expliqué por qué llegué tarde.
words.en: When telling the story, I explained why I arrived late.

words.es: Esa mañana estaba lloviendo y había mucho tráfico.
words.en: That morning it was raining and there was a lot of traffic.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing retell a journey with causes. Use the preterite for bounded events and connectors to order them; time words provide context. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use the preterite for bounded events and connectors to order them; time words provide context.

examples.es: Ayer llegué tarde a la estación.
examples.en: Yesterday I arrived late at the station.

examples.es: Primero busqué la salida correcta.
examples.en: First I looked for the correct exit.

lessons.title: Explain a change of routine
lessons.objective: Explain a change of routine: The imperfect frames habits and background; the preterite presents an event as bounded.

words.en: I normally used to have breakfast at home.

words.es: El lunes desayuné en la estación.
words.en: On Monday I had breakfast at the station.

words.es: Siempre llevaba un libro en la mochila.
words.en: I always used to carry a book in my backpack.
That day I forgot the backpack.

words.es: Mientras esperaba el tren, compré un periódico.
words.en: While I was waiting for the train, I bought a newspaper.

words.es: El viaje fue distinto de lo habitual.
words.en: The journey was different from the usual one.

words.es: Mi compañera me preguntó dónde estaba la mochila.
words.en: My coworker asked me where the backpack was.

words.es: Le dije que la había dejado en casa.
words.en: I told her that I had left it at home.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing explain a change of routine. The imperfect frames habits and background; the preterite presents an event as bounded. Both can describe the same situation from different viewpoints. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: The imperfect frames habits and background; the preterite presents an event as bounded. Both can describe the same situation from different viewpoints.

examples.es: Normalmente desayunaba en casa.
examples.en: I normally used to have breakfast at home.

examples.es: El lunes desayuné en la estación.
examples.en: On Monday I had breakfast at the station.

lessons.title: Describe an interrupted task
lessons.objective: Describe an interrupted task: Use imperfect for an action in progress and preterite for the interrupting event: leía cuando sonó.

words.es: Leía un mensaje cuando sonó el teléfono.
words.en: I was reading a message when the phone rang.

words.es: Mi hermana estaba en la puerta.
words.en: My sister was at the door.

words.es: Buscaba mis llaves cuando ella llamó otra vez.
words.en: I was looking for my keys when she called again.

words.es: Abrí la puerta y le pedí un minuto.
words.en: I opened the door and asked her for a minute.

words.es: Mientras ella esperaba, encontré las llaves.
words.en: While she was waiting, I found the keys.
We left together for the station.

words.es: Mi hermana quería saber si yo estaba listo.
words.en: My sister wanted to know whether I was ready.

words.es: Le expliqué que había perdido unos minutos buscando.
words.en: I explained that I had lost a few minutes searching.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing describe an interrupted task. Use imperfect for an action in progress and preterite for the interrupting event: leía cuando sonó. Cuando alone does not dictate a tense. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Use imperfect for an action in progress and preterite for the interrupting event: leía cuando sonó. Cuando alone does not dictate a tense.

examples.es: Leía un mensaje cuando sonó el teléfono.
examples.en: I was reading a message when the phone rang.

examples.es: Mi hermana estaba en la puerta.
examples.en: My sister was at the door.

lessons.title: Introduce a neighborhood over time
lessons.objective: Introduce a neighborhood over time: Desde names a starting point; desde hace names elapsed duration.

words.en: I have lived here since January.

words.es: Trabajo en la biblioteca desde hace dos meses.
words.en: I have worked at the library for two months.

words.es: Hace tres semanas conocí a mis vecinos.
words.en: I met my neighbors three weeks ago.

words.es: No veo a mi hermano desde el verano.
words.en: I have not seen my brother since the summer.
How long have you been studying Spanish?

words.es: Estudio español desde el año pasado.
words.en: I have been studying Spanish since last year.

words.es: En enero no conocía a nadie en el edificio.
words.en: In January I did not know anyone in the building.

words.es: Una vecina me invitó a tomar café.
words.en: A neighbor invited me to have coffee.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing introduce a neighborhood over time. Desde names a starting point; desde hace names elapsed duration. With an ongoing situation, Spanish often uses present where English uses have been. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Desde names a starting point; desde hace names elapsed duration. With an ongoing situation, Spanish often uses present where English uses have been.

examples.es: Vivo aquí desde enero.
examples.en: I have lived here since January.

examples.es: Trabajo en la biblioteca desde hace dos meses.
examples.en: I have worked at the library for two months.

lessons.title: Resolve a missing travel document
lessons.objective: Resolve a missing travel document: Lo, la, los and las replace a direct object and agree with its grammatical gender and number.

words.en: Do you have the hotel reservation?

words.es: Sí, la tengo en el teléfono.
words.en: Yes, I have it on my phone.
Where did you put the tickets?

words.es: Los puse dentro de la mochila.
words.en: I put them inside the backpack.

words.es: Necesito el pasaporte, pero no lo encuentro.
words.en: I need the passport, but I cannot find it.

words.es: Aquí está; lo dejaste sobre la mesa.
words.en: Here it is; you left it on the table.

words.es: Mi hermana me pidió que revisara todos los bolsillos.
words.en: My sister asked me to check all the pockets.

words.es: Ya los había revisado dos veces.
words.en: I had already checked them twice.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing resolve a missing travel document. Lo, la, los and las replace a direct object and agree with its grammatical gender and number. Put them before a conjugated verb. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Lo, la, los and las replace a direct object and agree with its grammatical gender and number. Put them before a conjugated verb.

examples.es: ¿Tienes la reserva del hotel?
examples.en: Do you have the hotel reservation?

examples.es: Sí, la tengo en el teléfono.
examples.en: Yes, I have it on my phone.

lessons.title: Clarify a recipient and an object
lessons.objective: Clarify a recipient and an object: Indirect precedes direct.
lessons.focus: Clarify a recipient and an object

words.es: Se lo voy a devolver esta tarde.
words.en: I am going to return it to her this afternoon.
And the photos of her children?

words.es: También se las voy a llevar.
words.en: I am also going to take them to her.

words.es: Marta me prestó el libro el lunes.
words.en: Marta lent me the book on Monday.
I want to give it to her before the trip.

words.es: Marta me preguntó si podía pasar por su oficina.
words.en: Marta asked me whether I could stop by her office.

words.es: Le dije que llevaría las fotos en una carpeta.
words.en: I told her I would bring the photos in a folder.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing clarify a recipient and an object. Indirect precedes direct. Le or les becomes se before lo, la, los or las; clarify the recipient when needed. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Indirect precedes direct. Le or les becomes se before lo, la, los or las; clarify the recipient when needed.

examples.es: Este libro es de Marta.
examples.en: This book belongs to Marta.

examples.es: Se lo voy a devolver esta tarde.
examples.en: I am going to return it to her this afternoon.

lessons.title: Negotiate a group preference
lessons.objective: Negotiate a group preference: The thing liked is the grammatical subject: me gusta el libro / me gustan los libros.

words.es: A mi amiga le interesa la historia.
words.en: My friend is interested in history.

words.es: Nos encanta conversar sobre los personajes.

words.en: Are you interested in our reading group?

words.es: Me gusta la idea, pero no me gustan las reuniones largas.
words.en: I like the idea, but I do not like long meetings.

words.es: Entonces te va a encantar nuestro horario.
words.en: Then you are going to love our schedule.

words.es: Una compañera propuso leer una novela larga.
words.en: A classmate suggested reading a long novel.

words.es: A mí me interesaba, pero no tenía tiempo suficiente.
words.en: I was interested, but I did not have enough time.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing negotiate a group preference. The thing liked is the grammatical subject: me gusta el libro / me gustan los libros. Interesar and encantar can follow the same pattern. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: The thing liked is the grammatical subject: me gusta el libro / me gustan los libros. Interesar and encantar can follow the same pattern.

examples.es: Me gustan las novelas cortas.
examples.en: I like short novels.

examples.es: A mi amiga le interesa la historia.
examples.en: My friend is interested in history.

lessons.title: Describe an accident without blame
lessons.objective: Describe an accident without blame: Se me cayó presents an event as accidental; the affected person appears as me, te, le, nos or les.

words.es: Se me cayó una taza en la cocina.
words.en: I accidentally dropped a cup in the kitchen.

words.es: La taza se rompió en el suelo.
words.en: The cup broke on the floor.

words.es: A mi hermano se le olvidó traer una toalla.
words.en: My brother forgot to bring a towel.
We cleaned up the water carefully.

words.es: Por suerte nadie se hizo daño.
Le expliqué a mi hermano que el suelo seguía mojado.
words.en: I explained to my brother that the floor was still wet.

words.es: Le pedí que no entrara hasta que terminara de limpiar.
words.en: I asked him not to enter until I finished cleaning.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing describe an accident without blame. Se me cayó presents an event as accidental; the affected person appears as me, te, le, nos or les. The verb agrees with the thing: se me cayeron las llaves. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Se me cayó presents an event as accidental; the affected person appears as me, te, le, nos or les. The verb agrees with the thing: se me cayeron las llaves.

examples.es: Se me cayó una taza en la cocina.
examples.en: I accidentally dropped a cup in the kitchen.

examples.es: La taza se rompió en el suelo.
examples.en: The cup broke on the floor.

lessons.title: Defend an apartment choice
lessons.objective: Defend an apartment choice: Más / menos .

words.es: Este apartamento es más luminoso que el otro.
words.en: This apartment is brighter than the other one.

words.es: La cocina es menos grande, pero está mejor equipada.
words.en: The kitchen is smaller, but it is better equipped.

words.es: El alquiler es tan caro como el anterior.
words.en: The rent is as expensive as the previous one.

words.es: Este es el edificio más tranquilo de la calle.
words.en: This is the quietest building on the street.

words.es: Para mí, la ubicación es la mejor ventaja.
words.en: For me, the location is the best advantage.

words.es: Tenemos que comparar también los gastos.
words.en: We also need to compare the expenses.

words.es: El dueño nos explicó qué gastos estaban incluidos.
words.en: The owner explained which expenses were included.

words.es: El otro apartamento tenía un alquiler más bajo.
words.en: The other apartment had lower rent.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing defend an apartment choice. Más / menos ... que compare; tan ... como states equality. Mejor and peor replace más bueno and más malo in ordinary comparisons; el más selects a group maximum. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Más / menos ... que compare; tan ... como states equality. Mejor and peor replace más bueno and más malo in ordinary comparisons; el más selects a group maximum.

examples.es: Este apartamento es más luminoso que el otro.
examples.en: This apartment is brighter than the other one.

examples.es: La cocina es menos grande, pero está mejor equipada.
examples.en: The kitchen is smaller, but it is better equipped.

lessons.title: Correct a shipping error
lessons.objective: Correct a shipping error: Para introduces a goal, recipient or deadline.

words.es: Este paquete es para mi hermana.
words.en: This package is for my sister.

words.es: Compré una caja para proteger el regalo.
words.en: I bought a box to protect the gift.

words.es: Pasé por la oficina de correos.
words.en: I went by the post office.

words.es: Pagué diez euros por el envío.
words.en: I paid ten euros for the shipping.

words.es: Gracias por ayudarme con la dirección.
words.en: Thank you for helping me with the address.

words.es: El empleado notó que faltaba el número del apartamento.
words.en: The employee noticed that the apartment number was missing.

words.es: Me pidió que lo escribiera en otra etiqueta.
words.en: He asked me to write it on another label.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing correct a shipping error. Para introduces a goal, recipient or deadline. Por can give cause, route or exchange. Learn the relationship in context rather than translating both as for. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Para introduces a goal, recipient or deadline. Por can give cause, route or exchange. Learn the relationship in context rather than translating both as for.

examples.es: Este paquete es para mi hermana.
examples.en: This package is for my sister.

examples.es: Lo necesito para el viernes.
examples.en: I need it by Friday.

lessons.title: Verify information from a notice
lessons.objective: Verify information from a notice: Nadie, nada and nunca before the verb need no extra no; after the verb they normally pair with no.

words.es: No hay nadie en la oficina.
words.en: There is nobody in the office.
I did not find any new message.
Do you have any news from the director?
No, I still do not know anything.

words.es: Nunca cerramos tan temprano los lunes.
words.en: We never close this early on Mondays.

words.es: Decidí no dejar un mensaje con datos privados.
words.en: I decided not to leave a message with private details.

words.es: Un compañero encontró un aviso en la puerta lateral.
words.en: A coworker found a notice on the side door.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing verify information from a notice. Nadie, nada and nunca before the verb need no extra no; after the verb they normally pair with no. Algún / ningún shorten before masculine singular nouns. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Nadie, nada and nunca before the verb need no extra no; after the verb they normally pair with no. Algún / ningún shorten before masculine singular nouns.

examples.es: No hay nadie en la oficina.
examples.en: There is nobody in the office.

examples.es: Nadie respondió al teléfono.
examples.en: Nobody answered the phone.

lessons.title: Plan around an uncertain forecast
lessons.objective: Plan around an uncertain forecast: The simple future adds endings to the infinitive, with irregular stems such as tendr- and har-.

words.es: El sábado visitaremos a nuestros primos.
words.en: On Saturday we will visit our cousins.

words.es: Vamos a salir temprano porque ya tenemos los boletos.
words.en: We are going to leave early because we already have the tickets.

words.es: Según el pronóstico, lloverá por la tarde.
words.en: According to the forecast, it will rain in the afternoon.
We will have to take umbrellas.
What will we do if they close the park?

words.es: Buscaremos un museo cerca del centro.
words.en: We will look for a museum near downtown.

words.es: Mis primos dijeron que el museo les parecía buena idea.
words.en: My cousins said that the museum seemed like a good idea to them.

words.es: Yo ya había buscado el horario de entrada.
words.en: I had already looked up the entrance hours.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing plan around an uncertain forecast. The simple future adds endings to the infinitive, with irregular stems such as tendr- and har-. Ir a + infinitive often emphasizes an existing plan. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: The simple future adds endings to the infinitive, with irregular stems such as tendr- and har-. Ir a + infinitive often emphasizes an existing plan.

examples.es: El sábado visitaremos a nuestros primos.
examples.en: On Saturday we will visit our cousins.

examples.es: Vamos a salir temprano porque ya tenemos los boletos.
examples.en: We are going to leave early because we already have the tickets.

lessons.title: Make a polite request and confirm it
lessons.objective: Make a polite request and confirm it: The conditional uses infinitive or future irregular stem plus -ía endings.
lessons.focus: Make a polite request and confirm it

words.es: Me gustaría quedarme una noche más.
words.en: I would like to stay one more night.
Would you have a quieter room?

words.es: Yo pediría una que no dé a la calle.
words.en: I would ask for one that does not face the street.

words.es: Sería mejor confirmar el precio primero.
words.en: It would be better to confirm the price first.

words.es: La recepcionista dijo que revisaría las opciones.
words.en: The receptionist said she would review the options.

words.es: La recepcionista encontró una habitación que daba al patio.
words.en: The receptionist found a room that faced the courtyard.

words.es: Nos explicó que costaría un poco más.
words.en: She explained that it would cost a little more.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing make a polite request and confirm it. The conditional uses infinitive or future irregular stem plus -ía endings. It can soften requests and offer advice; politeness also depends on context and intonation. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: The conditional uses infinitive or future irregular stem plus -ía endings. It can soften requests and offer advice; politeness also depends on context and intonation.

examples.es: ¿Podría cambiar mi reserva?
examples.en: Could I change my reservation?

examples.es: Me gustaría quedarme una noche más.
examples.en: I would like to stay one more night.

lessons.title: Report what has already been done
lessons.objective: Report what has already been done: With haber, participles stay unchanged: hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, abierto, puesto, vuelto and roto.
lessons.focus: Report what has already been done

words.es: He abierto la sala de reuniones.
words.en: I have opened the meeting room.

words.es: Ana ha puesto las carpetas sobre la mesa.
words.en: Ana has put the folders on the table.

words.es: El director ha dicho que llegará a las diez.
words.en: The director has said that he will arrive at ten.
Have you seen the new document?

words.es: Sí, y hemos hecho una copia para cada persona.
words.en: Yes, and we have made a copy for each person.

words.es: Cuando llegó el director, todos estábamos listos.
words.en: When the director arrived, we were all ready.

words.es: Él preguntó quién había preparado el resumen.
words.en: He asked who had prepared the summary.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing report what has already been done. With haber, participles stay unchanged: hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, abierto, puesto, vuelto and roto. Do not agree them with the subject or object. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: With haber, participles stay unchanged: hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, abierto, puesto, vuelto and roto. Do not agree them with the subject or object.

examples.es: He abierto la sala de reuniones.
examples.en: I have opened the meeting room.

examples.es: Ana ha puesto las carpetas sobre la mesa.
examples.en: Ana has put the folders on the table.

lessons.title: Teach a task with commands
lessons.objective: Teach a task with commands: Regular affirmative tú uses the él present form; common irregulars include di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten and ven.

words.es: Ven a mi casa a las nueve.
words.en: Come to my house at nine.

words.es: Trae una caja pequeña si tienes.
words.en: Bring a small box if you have one.

words.es: Pon los libros junto a la puerta.
words.en: Put the books next to the door.

words.es: Haz una lista de las cosas frágiles.
words.en: Make a list of the fragile things.

words.es: Después llama a Julia y dile que ya estamos listos.
words.en: Then call Julia and tell her that we are ready.

words.es: Mi amiga llegó antes que los demás.
words.en: My friend arrived before the others.

words.es: Le mostré dónde estaban las cosas más delicadas.
words.en: I showed her where the most delicate things were.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing teach a task with commands. Regular affirmative tú uses the él present form; common irregulars include di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten and ven. Attached pronouns may require an accent. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Regular affirmative tú uses the él present form; common irregulars include di, haz, ve, pon, sal, sé, ten and ven. Attached pronouns may require an accent.

examples.es: Ven a mi casa a las nueve.
examples.en: Come to my house at nine.

examples.es: Trae una caja pequeña si tienes.
examples.en: Bring a small box if you have one.

lessons.title: Give formal directions clearly
lessons.objective: Give formal directions clearly: Usted and ustedes commands use the corresponding present subjunctive.

words.es: Pase por esta puerta, por favor.
Deje la mochila en el casillero.
words.en: Leave your backpack in the locker.
Do not touch the works of art.

words.es: Si vienen en grupo, esperen junto a la escalera.
words.en: If you come as a group, wait next to the stairs.

words.es: Pregunten al personal si necesitan ayuda.
words.en: Ask the staff if you need help.

words.es: Una visitante preguntó dónde podía dejar el cochecito.
words.en: A visitor asked where she could leave the stroller.

words.es: El empleado le indicó un espacio junto a la recepción.
words.en: The employee pointed out a space next to reception.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing give formal directions clearly. Usted and ustedes commands use the corresponding present subjunctive. No keeps the same form; compare pase and no pase. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Usted and ustedes commands use the corresponding present subjunctive. No keeps the same form; compare pase and no pase.

examples.es: Pase por esta puerta, por favor.
examples.en: Go through this door, please.

examples.es: Deje la mochila en el casillero.
examples.en: Leave your backpack in the locker.

lessons.title: Express wishes without changing subjects
lessons.objective: Express wishes without changing subjects: A wish such as quiero que with a new subject normally takes the subjunctive.

words.es: Quiero que mis padres conozcan la ciudad.
words.en: I want my parents to get to know the city.

words.es: Espero que el viaje sea tranquilo.
words.en: I hope the trip is peaceful.

words.es: Mi madre quiere visitar el mercado.
words.en: My mother wants to visit the market.

words.es: Mi padre prefiere que salgamos temprano.
words.en: My father prefers us to leave early.

words.es: Deseo que todos tengan tiempo para descansar.
words.en: I wish everyone had time to rest.

words.es: Yo quiero preparar una cena en casa.
words.en: I want to prepare dinner at home.

words.es: Mis padres me preguntaron qué quería hacer primero.
words.en: My parents asked me what I wanted to do first.

words.es: Yo quería caminar sin un horario fijo.
words.en: I wanted to walk without a fixed schedule.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing express wishes without changing subjects. A wish such as quiero que with a new subject normally takes the subjunctive. With one subject, use an infinitive: quiero ir; quiero que vayas. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: A wish such as quiero que with a new subject normally takes the subjunctive. With one subject, use an infinitive: quiero ir; quiero que vayas.

examples.es: Quiero que mis padres conozcan la ciudad.
examples.en: I want my parents to get to know the city.

examples.es: Espero que el viaje sea tranquilo.
examples.en: I hope the trip is peaceful.

lessons.title: Check a doubtful claim with evidence
lessons.objective: Check a doubtful claim with evidence: Dudo que and no creo que commonly introduce subjunctive; creo que normally introduces indicative.
lessons.focus: Check a doubtful claim with evidence

words.es: Creo que la biblioteca abre el sábado.
words.en: I think the library opens on Saturday.

words.es: No creo que cierre tan temprano.
words.en: I do not think it closes so early.

words.es: Dudo que ese anuncio sea reciente.
words.en: I doubt that that notice is recent.

words.es: Es posible que hayan cambiado el horario.
words.en: It is possible that they have changed the schedule.

words.es: Sabemos que el sitio web tiene un número de teléfono.
words.en: We know that the website has a phone number.
Let us call to confirm the information.

words.es: La persona que atendió confirmó que el aviso era antiguo.
words.en: The person who answered confirmed that the notice was old.

words.es: Nos dijo que la biblioteca cerraba una hora más tarde.
words.en: She told us that the library closed an hour later.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing check a doubtful claim with evidence. Dudo que and no creo que commonly introduce subjunctive; creo que normally introduces indicative. Choose the mood from the speaker's stance, not from que alone. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Dudo que and no creo que commonly introduce subjunctive; creo que normally introduces indicative. Choose the mood from the speaker's stance, not from que alone.

examples.en: I think the library opens on Saturday.

examples.es: No creo que cierre tan temprano.
examples.en: I do not think it closes so early.

lessons.title: Compare a real plan with a hypothesis
lessons.objective: Compare a real plan with a hypothesis: For an open condition about the future, si normally takes present indicative; the result may use future, present or a command.
lessons.focus: Compare a real plan with a hypothesis

words.es: Si hace buen tiempo, iremos al parque.
words.en: If the weather is good, we will go to the park.
If it rains, we will eat at home.
If you have a blanket, bring it.

words.es: Podemos comprar fruta si la tienda está abierta.
words.en: We can buy fruit if the store is open.

words.es: Si vienen tus primos, habrá comida suficiente.
words.en: If your cousins come, there will be enough food.

words.es: Te llamaré si cambia el plan.
words.en: I will call you if the plan changes.

words.es: Mi primo preguntó qué haríamos con una tarde libre.
words.en: My cousin asked what we would do with a free afternoon.

words.es: Si tuviéramos más tiempo, visitaríamos también el lago.
words.en: If we had more time, we would also visit the lake.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing compare a real plan with a hypothesis. For an open condition about the future, si normally takes present indicative; the result may use future, present or a command. Avoid future immediately after conditional si. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: For an open condition about the future, si normally takes present indicative; the result may use future, present or a command. Avoid future immediately after conditional si.

examples.es: Si hace buen tiempo, iremos al parque.
examples.en: If the weather is good, we will go to the park.

examples.es: Si llueve, comeremos en casa.
examples.en: If it rains, we will eat at home.

lessons.title: Explain a decision and answer an objection
lessons.objective: Explain a decision and answer an objection: Aunque introduces a concession; sin embargo contrasts statements; por eso gives a consequence.
lessons.focus: Explain a decision and answer an objection

words.es: El curso es corto; sin embargo, exige práctica diaria.
words.en: The course is short; however, it requires daily practice.

words.es: Aunque trabajo por la mañana, puedo asistir por la tarde.
words.en: Although I work in the morning, I can attend in the afternoon.

words.es: Las clases son pequeñas, por eso todos participan.
words.en: The classes are small, so everyone participates.

words.es: Además, el centro está cerca de mi casa.
words.en: Also, the center is near my home.

words.es: El precio incluye los materiales, pero no el transporte.
words.en: The price includes the materials, but not transportation.
For these reasons, I decided to enroll.

words.es: Mi hermano pensaba que el curso sería demasiado intenso.
words.en: My brother thought the course would be too intensive.

words.es: Le expliqué que podía elegir un grupo de fin de semana.
words.en: I explained that I could choose a weekend group.

lessons.speaking: You and a Spanish-speaking classmate are discussing explain a decision and answer an objection. Aunque introduces a concession; sin embargo contrasts statements; por eso gives a consequence. Indicative aunque can present an accepted fact. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

grammar.focus: Aunque introduces a concession; sin embargo contrasts statements; por eso gives a consequence. Indicative aunque can present an accepted fact.

examples.es: El curso es corto; sin embargo, exige práctica diaria.
examples.en: The course is short; however, it requires daily practice.

examples.es: Aunque trabajo por la mañana, puedo asistir por la tarde.
examples.en: Although I work in the morning, I can attend in the afternoon.
